prompt_text:
Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that streams audio chunks from an async source using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 2 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 3 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 4 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 5 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 6 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import asyncio
import os
from deepgram import (
    DeepgramClient,
    LiveTranscriptionEvents,
    LiveOptions,
)

# A dummy async audio source that yields silent audio chunks.
# In a real application, this would come from a microphone or a network stream.
async def get_audio_source():
    """
    An async generator that yields chunks of silent audio data.
    """
    chunk_size = 1024 * 2  # 2 KB chunks
    # Simulate sending audio for a few seconds
    for _ in range(100):
        # This example sends silent audio. In a real application, you would
        # replace this with actual audio data from your source.
        yield b'\x00' * chunk_size
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # Simulate real-time audio chunk arrival

async def transcribe_streaming_from_async_source():
    """
    Streams audio from an async generator to Deepgram and prints the transcription.
    """
    try:
        api_key = os.getenv("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY")
        if not api_key:
            raise ValueError("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

        deepgram = DeepgramClient(api_key)
        dg_connection = deepgram.listen.asynclive.v("1")

        async def on_open(self, open, **kwargs):
            print(f"--- Connection opened ---")

        async def on_message(self, result, **kwargs):
            transcript = result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript
            if len(transcript) > 0:
                print(f"Transcription: {transcript}")

        async def on_error(self, error, **kwargs):
            print(f"--- Error: {error} ---")

        async def on_close(self, close, **kwargs):
            print(f"--- Connection closed ---")

        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Open, on_open)
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Transcript, on_message)
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Error, on_error)
        dg_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Close, on_close)

        options = LiveOptions(
            model="nova-2",
            language="en-US",
            smart_format=True,
        )

        if await dg_connection.start(options) is False:
            print("Failed to start Deepgram connection.")
            return

        # Get the async audio source and send data
        async for audio_chunk in get_audio_source():
            await dg_connection.send(audio_chunk)

        await dg_connection.finish()

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # To run this script, set the DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable.
    # e.g., export DEEPGRAM_API_KEY='your_deepgram_api_key'
    # Because this example uses a dummy audio source of silence, it will not
    # produce any meaningful transcription output.
    asyncio.run(transcribe_streaming_from_async_source())
